summary: Sahand Airport (ACP/OITM) is a small regional airport serving the city of Maragheh in East Azerbaijan Province, northwestern Iran. It is named after Mount Sahand, a massive dormant stratovolcano that dominates the region's skyline. The airport primarily handles domestic flights connecting Maragheh to major Iranian cities including Tehran and serves visitors drawn to the area's rich Ilkhanid-era history.
faqs:
Q: What cities can I fly to from Sahand Airport?
A: The airport operates primarily domestic flights, with regular service to Tehran (Mehrabad Airport) and occasional connections to other major Iranian cities.

Q: How far is the airport from Maragheh city center?
A: Sahand Airport is located approximately 10 kilometers northwest of central Maragheh, typically a 15-20 minute drive.

Q: Is the airport open for international flights?
A: No, Sahand Airport is a domestic-only facility. International travelers must fly into larger hubs like Tabriz or Tehran.

Q: When is the best time to visit Maragheh?
A: Spring (April-May) and early autumn offer pleasant weather for exploring the region, including Mount Sahand and the famous Maragheh Observatory ruins.
transport_tips: Taxis are the most reliable way to reach the airport, and it's advisable to arrange a return ride through your hotel in advance. Ride-sharing apps like Snapp and Tapsi operate in Maragheh and can serve the airport, though availability may be limited compared to larger cities. The road from Maragheh to the airport is well-maintained and straightforward.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time, visit the ruins of the Maragheh Observatory, built in 1259 under the Ilkhanid ruler Hulagu Khan. It is one of the most significant astronomical sites of the medieval Islamic world and is just a short drive from the city center.
